A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ETGL-DDPG and provide readable main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The complete 23-page v1 and 28-page v2 support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original continuous-control experiments, exploration coverage, component ablations, and appendix analyses comparing perfect-model exploration and terminal-state distributions.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds component-combination experiments, HER and averaged-return comparisons, and option-length distributions.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 and Algorithms 1–3 retain the same replay-based tree search, adaptive GDRB sampling, and longest n-step updates. HER and avg8-step are evaluated as alternatives; the proposed ETGL-DDPG procedure is not revised.

E1.justification: Both versions use Wall-maze, U-maze, Point-push, soccer, window-open, and button-press with the same task requirements. The added component comparisons use existing navigation environments.

E2.justification: v2 adds DDPG+HER versus DDPG+GDRB in Figure 8 and compares the avg8-step rule from Meng et al. within ETGL-DDPG against longest returns in Figure 9. These targeted additions retain the primary DDPG, SAC, TD3, and DOIE comparator set.

E3.justification: New controlled experiments replace omitted components with their standard DDPG counterparts and substitute averaged 1–8-step returns for longest returns. Figure 5 additionally measures option-length frequencies. Existing training budgets, architectures, environment settings, and hyperparameter tables are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's individual-component tests, v2 adds all three two-component combinations, option-length distributions, and direct HER/GDRB and avg8/longest-return analyses. These substantially expand investigation of component interactions and alternatives. The existing budget sweep moves to Appendix A.7 rather than being newly added.

E5.justification: Both retain five-run performance reporting and ten-run exploration-coverage reporting with one-standard-deviation bands. The new Figure 6 follows the existing five-run practice; no increased retained run counts or new confidence-interval or significance-testing procedures are reported.

E6.justification: Under unchanged reported benchmark settings, Figure 3 revises DOIE's Wall-maze trajectory and lowers its late Point-push success from roughly 1 to 0.85. Figure 4 changes coverage levels and now identifies epsilon-z-greedy as fastest to full U-maze coverage. Perfect-model curves also change between v1 Figure 6 and v2 Figure 10. Figures 5, 6, 8, and 9 add findings; the relocated budget-sweep values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Definitions 1–3, Theorems 1–2, and Appendix A.1's proofs remain substantively identical. Corrections to the optimal-policy label and option-distribution notation do not change the mathematical criteria, bounds, or reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contribution statements retain the three-component DDPG enhancement, polynomial sample-complexity claim, and superiority across tested benchmarks. Calling the components orthogonal and adding supporting experiments do not substantively redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: The conclusion newly states that epsilon-t-greedy and GDRB require adaptation for stochastic environments. New interpretations attribute avg8-step's faster convergence to averaging and HER's early learning advantage to additional reward guidance; Section 4.2 also discusses the option-length distribution's relationship to zeta distributions.

D1.justification: Hardware, architecture, hyperparameters, and implementation-access information are retained. However, v2 Section 5 newly assigns reservoir sampling to GDRB's success-event buffer, contradicting the retained FIFO specification in Section 3.2. This changes the technical documentation without establishing an implementation change.

R1.justification: v2 adds Go-Explore, SSET, SORS, and additional DDPG-related references, while developing explicit comparisons with Tang's hashing approach and Eysenbach's replay-buffer graph. Newly positioning GDRB relative to a single-goal-event interpretation of SSET substantially expands discussion of its relationship to prior work.

P1.justification: The introduction is locally rewritten, related work is divided into four topics, and the budget discussion moves from Section 4.2 to Appendix A.7. Appendix organization expands, while the central section sequence, method exposition, and proof narrative remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 changes typography, headings, author-block layout, and document flow. It adds four multi-panel figures—Figures 5, 6, 8, and 9—and rearranges existing displays, including moving the budget-sweep table from the main text into the appendix.

improvement.justification: The new pairwise ablations and HER/avg8 controls improve evidence for component choices and tradeoffs, while the deterministic-domain caveat clarifies applicability. These gains are moderated by new reporting inconsistencies: Section 5 contradicts Section 3.2 about buffer retention, and Section 4.2 reports 80%/60% Wall-maze coverage although Figure 4 plateaus near 90%/70%. The added scrutiny supports a limited net quality improvement.
